title: Week Ahead — Market Outlook
headline: Equities enter a data- and earnings-heavy week with subdued headline volatility but asymmetric downside risk from geopolitics, Treasury supply, and policy surprises.
volatilityRationale: The latest VIX reading is near 15, keeping the headline volatility regime relatively calm, while Cboe says S&P 500 skew collapsed to a one-year low as investors chased upside and sold hedges. That calm meets a dense event slate—FOMC minutes, retail earnings, Treasury auctions, PMIs, and unresolved Middle East tensions—so a volatility pickup remains a credible scenario.

recap.text: The S&P 500 fell 0.17% on Friday from a record close, while the Nasdaq fell 0.28% and the Dow fell 0.20%; for the week, the S&P 500 gained 0.4% and the Nasdaq 0.1%, while the Dow lost 0.6%.

A softer-than-expected July producer-price report helped the S&P 500 set a record close on Thursday and reduced near-term rate-hike fears, though the market remains sensitive to the next inflation and labor signals.
July retail sales unexpectedly fell 0.6% and early-August consumer sentiment weakened, while U.S.-Iran tensions lifted oil prices and kept inflation and growth risks in play.
The latest available Cboe quote showed VIX at 14.92 on August 17, up 0.67 from the prior close of 14.25, a low absolute level but a reminder that volatility can reprice quickly around catalysts.

triggers.text: Empire State manufacturing and NAHB housing-market indexes open the week with early reads on regional activity and housing sentiment.
Housing starts, import and export prices, industrial production, capacity utilization, pending home sales, and Home Depot and Keysight earnings create a dense Tuesday macro-and-consumer test.
The Federal Reserve releases minutes from its July 28–29 meeting, alongside results from TJX, Analog Devices, Target, Lowe’s, and other retailers and industrial companies.
Initial jobless claims, the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index, leading indicators, and Walmart, Deere, and Ross Stores earnings will test the consumer and cyclical-growth narrative.
Preliminary S&P Global manufacturing and services PMIs provide the week’s final broad read on private-sector momentum and price pressure.

watch.text: VIX and the shape of the volatility curve: a move away from the latest near-15 spot reading would signal that the market is repricing the event cluster.

S&P 500 downside protection: Cboe reported that SPX skew collapsed to a one-year low as investors sold hedges and chased upside, leaving less visible protection if geopolitics or rates shock the tape.

Treasury supply and funding conditions: the Treasury schedule includes bill auctions beginning August 17, while the market is still digesting the prior week’s $125 billion quarterly-refunding auctions.

Whether earnings validate AI-capex optimism and consumer resilience: investors are looking to corporate results for direction before the Jackson Hole symposium later this month and Nvidia’s earnings the following week.
